Preserves the MIT-licensed VulkanMemoryAllocator header from the former SDK submodule at AMD commit 1d8f600fd424278486eade7ed3e877c99f0846b1, unchanged; prefer it when resolving VMA so a clean v0.11 checkout does not depend on an untracked old submodule or a host-specific Vulkan SDK package layout.
patches.test: Release Vulkan configuration from clean patch replay; Native/Xenos Vulkan compilation and real-GPU preflight

patches.note: Restores the official pre-removal CAS, FSR multipass and experimental FSR2/3 presenter paths and shader assets from a795de17^ into the v0.11 Xenos/Native host boundary. Preserves canonical settings, module providers, overlays and shared ownership; carries original Xenia/AMD BSD/MIT credits and uses the existing pinned FidelityFX checkout. Rebuild matching GPU modules. Runtime/real-pixel validation remains required.
patches.test: tests/unit/gpu/xenos_base_test.cpp; tests/sdkcheck/presenter_effects_test.cpp; tests/native/probe.cpp; tests/native/vulkan_probe.cpp; matched presenter pixel and multipass regression required

patches.note: Routes the existing composed-output diagnostic through the official graphics system and driver, shared by Xenos and Native. Preserves actual presenter readback without exposing private runtime/driver pointers; updates the graphics interface identity for the changed driver ABI.

Binds the canonical presentation SRV heap before every graphics effect, including after FidelityFX temporal dispatches. Restores the required D3D12 state without skipping effects or changing pixels/timing. The real-GPU synthetic presenter contract reproduces the original NVIDIA access violation at SetGraphicsRootDescriptorTable without title content.

Restores the pre-runtime input validation and revision-isolated cache boundary on the official App lifecycle. Runs after all user layers and before driver creation or startup freeze; failures unwind normal initialization. No second runtime or launcher.
patches.test: tests/sdkcheck/session_title_app_test.cpp (settled settings and dashboard path contracts)

patches.note: Exports the existing canonical task cancellation predicate and retained-handle release used by original system workers. Preserves implementation, cancellation, references, nested task identity and original TLS fallback without introducing task state or a runtime.

Adds a scoped cleanup boundary to the single official TitleRuntime after guest threads stop and before XAM, modules and memory release. Covers failed Launch and normal shutdown; replacement guards cannot remove a newer registration. Required for original Guide host lifetime without a parallel runtime.
patches.test: tests/sdkcheck/session_title_app_test.cpp (failed graphics attach, guest exit, host close and unload observer lifetime)

patches.note: Exposes the existing original achievement ledger through the official XAM title-services interface, versioned to 11. Guide notification metadata reads the same committed per-account store as guest writes, without substituting the host achievement facade or creating another storage model.

Exports existing XAM message dispatch, I/O cancellation and content callback registration bodies for original-system diagnostic hooks. No operation, synchronization or state is reimplemented; direct canonical calls avoid hook recursion on ELF.

Makes the existing canonical raw dispatcher operation public for integrations that consume original PowerPC vector and floating-point outputs. Execute in v0.11 restores the register file, unlike v0.10. No ABI frame, thread binding or execution implementation is duplicated.

Exposes the single title-owned physical memory, write-watch and guest-interrupt interfaces to headless Native capture replay. Constructs the existing lightweight TitleContext at successful Load rather than AttachSystems, then passes that same object to graphics. No duplicate context, memory, threads or runtime; listener guards retain their existing teardown contract.

Desktop content tools use the canonical base and filesystem modules as static libraries without configuring title, kernel or GPU libraries. Full SDK builds remain unchanged. The LGPL LZX decoder stays a separate replaceable shared library; the host owns the canonical allocator and filesystem module.

The XAM context and public workspace service retain the title-owned ITitleWorkspace facade instead of a WorkspaceHeap that SetExecutableModule can replace after reading the XEX workspace-size header. Delegates to the single current allocator with unchanged size, zeroing, budget, errors and allocation semantics. Prevents generic XamAlloc/XamFree use-after-free for nondefault workspace headers; no title-specific behavior or second allocator/runtime.

Retains the guest processor-4 affinity from original patch 0071 using the official KernelThread creation mask. Original mixers select per-processor callback buffers; default processor 0 is not equivalent. Preserves the existing APU, callback frame, arguments, FP policy and audio timing without a second runtime or renderer.

Retains original patch 0071 callback-before-thread-retirement ordering with the single canonical APU worker. Serializes the callback selection gate, lets the current callback finish with its decoder and streams available, avoids self-join for callback-originated title exits, and reuses upstream bounded wait/stop handling for blocked callbacks. No second runtime, dropped audio frames or changed mixing/sample timing.

Uses the existing IFileSystemFactory native stat operation to reject oversized local save/profile thumbnails before opening or allocating their payload. Keeps ERROR_INVALID_DATA for known oversized metadata on Windows even under an exclusive file handle, and preserves missing/unreadable/directory errors plus the bounded read against growth after the snapshot. No title-specific behavior or weakened output validation.

Publishes the canonical UI focus, audio focus and input capture state before delivering a focus notification. The v0.11.0 listener API has no focus payload, so observers must read the current state through IUISystem::IsFocused. Preserves event order and the original SDL focus integration without another runtime, renderer or input path.

Compares achievement toast expiry with the exact clock duration. Conversion to float before scaling loses nanosecond precision at 4.5 seconds, delaying detachment and later queued events. Keeps the original visible lifetime and fade effects.

Allows the existing recompile-tests tool to exercise the production fast vector math path explicitly. Official hardware-reference tests keep exact math by default; the local VMX overflow/NaN regression keeps its fast-path contract. No title compiler or runtime defaults change.
patches.test: tests/sdkcheck/vmsum/main.cpp; official ppc_tests exact hardware reference cases

llvm.why: ReXGlue v0.10.0 CMakeLists.txt rejects non-Clang compilers and Clang < 18; official win-amd64 CI installs upstream LLVM. 22.1.8 was the newest stable LLVM when v0.10.0 was tagged (2026-08-21).

llvm_windows_arm64.why: Same LLVM release as llvm, native Windows ARM64 host build (GitHub release asset digest); selected on ARM64 Windows hosts.
